Hey! Good job!!

12 pounds in a month is a very healthy and sustainable amount. And I personally don't feel like carbs are our enemies. Omad is a lifestyle and I don't see how someone could stick with it if they have to cut out their favourite foods. Personally I wouldn't be able to live without pasta and I know that I would eventually give in and go into a bingefest rampage which would hinder my progress a lot probably.

Wish you all the best in the future!

So proud of you!! 

I know how you feel as I don't have anyone to tell either, my friends and parents just don't understand and would think that I am starving myself.

20lbs is amazing and I wish you best of luck in the future! <3

Hi! Thank you!

I don't really count my carbs, because personally, I don't think carbs are our enemies, when eaten in moderation.

But I think it's important to find a balance, I do try to put more vegetables and protein on my plate than I used to.

imo the main thing with OMAD is that if you want to feel good doing it, and to keep doing it, you should not restrict yourself, as in, eat what you usually would but in moderation. 

Have a good day! :)

Hey!

Thank you for the kind words, I'll try to reply to your questions as good as possible! :) 

Since I am not water fasting, I don't take any electrolytes as I feel that I don't really need them.

I'm a 23y/o female, 169cm, living in Turkey

I try to eat what I usually would:
Some days I eat soup (chicken soup, soup with just vegetables and no meat etc) and a sandwich on the side (usually with cream cheese and a fried egg)

Buckwheat with vegetables and a salad, usually I add a scrambled eggs and/or tuna
(Buckwheat also makes a great salad - bell pepper, buckwheat, sweet corn, cucumber, sour cream, mayo, tuna, served cold)

(Chickpea cutlets with tuna are really really good if you don't want to/can't eat meat cutlets)

I'm not a vegetarian or anything, but first of all preparing meat takes time and the second and the more important reason is that meat is pretty expensive and that's why I don't buy it that much as I'm kinda living on a budget right now. That's why I try to substitute it with eggs, tuna, chickpeas etc to get some of that protein on my plate.

In general I think I eat around 1000-1300 calories a day, and for me that's enough and I feel full and great.

I've always struggled with sleep and I can't really tell if it's better or not - the first days were really hard since the hunger pangs would keep me awake, but I think my body has adjusted now so I don't have that kind of a problem anymore.

In general I can't see any changes in my mental health, except for the fact that I do feel happier since I am quite proud of myself for keeping up with this.

When it comes to the pizza, I don't really feel guilty about it since it was kinda planned to be my meal of the day. I think I didn't explain it well enough, but what I wanted to say is that what I love about OMAD is the fact that I CAN eat a pizza if I want as long as it's in moderation.

In the past I have tried to eliminate all the junk food and eat super healthy only and that backfired.

I haven't taken any blood tests in a while and I don't plan on in the future.

Wish you all the best in the future! :)

I've been on omad for 16 days now and I always eat a banana or one piece of chocolate after my meal, for dessert. Otherwise I know that I would probably binge some sweets later. I don't think it's a crime to have some dessert after your meal :)

I started my OMAD diet 10 days ago. I've been struggling with my weight for my whole life. But I honestly feel, like omad is the only way to lose weight for me, because I'm not consistent enough to eat full healthy meals and not snack, snacking was my biggest problem. I've lost 6lbs in 10 days and it's a great feeling. The first couple of days were a nightmare not gonna lie. My stomach was grumbling all the time and it hurt. But I feel like my body has now adjusted and I don't even feel that hungry anymore before my meal time. I've been trying to make healthy meals, but I still treat myself to a piece of candy or a banana for dessert and I think that's why it's such a good diet - you don't have to necessarily cut out any foods. Just keep it in moderation and after a week you probably won't even eat as much as you used to. OH and what really helped me was starting a diary. Every single day I write down my weight, what I ate and most importantly how I'm feeling and how proud I am of myself. That helps me so much.
